quote: I have never recovered my respect for committee decisions in matters of initiation.
Yeats fought bravely at my side to reclaim the Order's papers from Mathers.
why: Excerpt says the opposite: Yeats was among those who refused Crowley's initiation and wrote against him to Mathers; the London members (not Crowley and Yeats together) locked out Mathers's side.

quote: The Golden Dawn's inner conflicts reflected broader tensions in the occult revival of the 1900s.
why: A plausible-sounding generalization the excerpt (a personal, specific account of one schism) never makes or supports either way.

quote: Every adept who has learned to read the Astral Light reads, in effect, the whole history of the world.
why: Verbatim closing line of the excerpt.

quote: Blavatsky rejected Eliphas Levi's concept of the Magical Agent as worthless superstition.
why: Excerpt says the opposite: she credits Levi ('He was right to name it so') and builds on his concept rather than rejecting it.

quote: The Rishis of the Upanishads possessed more astral knowledge than any Western tradition.
why: Excerpt mentions the Rishis/Upanishads only in passing as a source that also knew the astral principle; it makes no comparative superiority claim over Western traditions.

quote: the Signature stands in the Essence, and is as a Lute that lies still
Bohme argued the Signature was purely a spiritual entity with no connection to Nature's essence.
why: Excerpt says the opposite: 'the Signature or Form is no Spirit, but the Receptacle... of the Spirit, wherein it lies... the Signature stands in the Essence.'

quote: Bohme's craft metaphors in this chapter directly influenced later Rosicrucian symbolism.
why: Excerpt uses a lute/instrument metaphor but says nothing about Rosicrucian influence or reception history one way or the other.

quote: I wrote this work in twelve days.
Dee admitted the sign of the Monad was a mere allegorical device with no literal unifying power.
why: Excerpt says the opposite: 'This is not metaphor... Those who think I am speaking of correspondences have not yet understood me. I am speaking of identities.'

quote: Dee considered twelve days a mystically significant number for completing such a work.
why: Excerpt states the twelve-day timeframe but frames it as evidence the knowledge 'arrives entire, not built up laboriously' rather than assigning numerological significance to twelve itself.

quote: Blake insisted that the Body and Soul were entirely separate, opposing substances.
why: Excerpt says the opposite as one of its stated 'Contraries': 'Man has no Body distinct from his Soul.'

work: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
quote: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell directly critiques the Church of England's doctrine of original sin.
why: Excerpt criticizes 'Bibles or sacred codes' and the restraint of Energy/Desire in general terms; it names no specific church or doctrine of original sin.

quote: the imagination is not nonexistent, even though it has no real external existence
why: Verbatim opening line of the excerpt. Same case #153's original ad hoc check (scripts/test-library-grounding.js, now superseded by this harness) used.

quote: Ibn Arabi taught that the imagination must be abolished entirely for the mystic to reach unity with God.
why: Excerpt says the opposite: 'the mystic who knows this does not need to abolish forms to reach unity.'

quote: Ibn Arabi's teaching on imagination in this passage directly shaped later Sufi lodges' initiation rites.
why: Excerpt is a metaphysical argument about imagination and form; it says nothing about institutional transmission into lodge initiation practice.
